newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down despite a rally in OTCs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down despite a rally in OTCs.

text.p: The Singapore share index finished down on Friday on a dull day despite a pre-National Day rally in Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks.
Malaysia is celebrating its National Day on Saturday.
However, the lack of trading interest was evident in the slackening of interest in second liners and blue chips trailing even further behind, dealers said.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 9.11 points to 2,153.54 in line with Wall Street's overnight fall.
Market volume was a thin 81.52 million shares with losers leading gainers by 186 to 112.
Malaysian Resources was the most actively traded stock with 4.61 million shares changing hands, including a block deal of 3.7 million shares. It was down Singapore $0.08 at S$4.36.
Kemayan Corp gained S$0.12 to S$1.80 on a heavy volume of 4.05 million shares.
Blue chips Cerebos and Singapore Land were among the losers, each dropping S$0.30 to S$11.70 and S$9.10 respectively.
Top gainer was Keppel Corp, rising S$0.30 to S$10.70.
